name: Fisher-Tippett-Gnedenko theorem
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.IsExtremeValueDistr.classification
  {G : CumulativeDistributionFunction} (G_evd : G.IsExtremeValueDistr) :
  (∃ A, A • G = standardGumbelCDF) ∨
    (∃ A α, ∃ (hα : 0 < α), A • G = standardFrechetCDF hα) ∨
      ∃ A α, ∃ (hα : 0 < α), A • G = standardWeibullCDF hα
scope_note: No extra hypotheses. Says every extreme value law is of Gumbel, Fréchet or Weibull type; it does not assert the normalizing constants of any particular F (that is the domains area).

name: Fisher-Tippett-Gnedenko, Jenkinson-von Mises form
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.IsExtremeValueDistr.exists_smul_eq_gevCDF
  {G : CumulativeDistributionFunction} (hG : G.IsExtremeValueDistr) :
  ∃ A ξ, A • G = ExtremeValueTheory.gevCDF ξ
scope_note: Every extreme value law is of the type of a standard GEV law H_xi. Location and scale are carried by the affine map.

name: Max-stable laws are the extreme value laws
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isMaxStable_iff_isExtremeValueDistr
  (G : CumulativeDistributionFunction) : G.IsMaxStable ↔ G.IsExtremeValueDistr
scope_note: Nothing left out. Univariate; multivariate max-stability is in the multivariate area.

name: The standard Gumbel law is an extreme value law
statement: isExtremeValueDistr_standardGumbelCDF : standardGumbelCDF.IsExtremeValueDistr
scope_note: Standard form only; other members of the type follow from the affine action.

name: The standard Fréchet law is an extreme value law
statement:
isExtremeValueDistr_standardFrechetCDF {ξ : ℝ} (ξ_pos : 0 < ξ) :
  (standardFrechetCDF ξ_pos).IsExtremeValueDistr
scope_note: Standard form only, for every shape > 0.

name: The standard Weibull law is an extreme value law
statement:
isExtremeValueDistr_standardWeibullCDF {ξ : ℝ} (ξ_pos : 0 < ξ) :
  (standardWeibullCDF ξ_pos).IsExtremeValueDistr
scope_note: Standard form only, for every shape > 0.

name: Mean of the GEV law, xi != 0
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.integral_id_gevCDF {ξ : ℝ} (hξ : ξ < 1) (h0 : ξ ≠ 0) :
  ∫ (x : ℝ), x ∂(ExtremeValueTheory.gevCDF ξ).measure = (Real.Gamma (1 - ξ) - 1) / ξ
scope_note: Standard law (location 0, scale 1), for xi < 1, xi != 0. The value at xi = 0 is the separate entry gev-mean-zero. Integrability is proved.

name: Variance of the GEV law, xi != 0
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.variance_id_gevCDF {ξ : ℝ} (hξ : ξ < 1 / 2) (h0 : ξ ≠ 0) :
  ProbabilityTheory.variance (fun x => x) (ExtremeValueTheory.gevCDF ξ).measure =
    (Real.Gamma (1 - 2 * ξ) - Real.Gamma (1 - ξ) ^ 2) / ξ ^ 2
scope_note: Standard law, for xi < 1/2, xi != 0. The value at xi = 0 is the separate entry gumbel-variance.

name: The mean of the Gumbel law is Euler's constant
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.integral_id_gevCDF_zero :
  ∫ (x : ℝ), x ∂(ExtremeValueTheory.gevCDF 0).measure = Real.eulerMascheroniConstant
scope_note: Standard law.

name: The variance of the Gumbel law is pi^2/6
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.variance_id_gevCDF_zero :
  ProbabilityTheory.variance (fun x => x) (ExtremeValueTheory.gevCDF 0).measure = Real.pi ^ 2 / 6
scope_note: Standard law.

name: Probability-weighted moments of the GEV law
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.integral_mul_gevFun_pow_gevCDF {ξ : ℝ} (hξ : ξ < 1) (h0 : ξ ≠ 0) (r : ℕ) :
  ∫ (x : ℝ), x * ExtremeValueTheory.gevFun ξ x ^ r ∂(ExtremeValueTheory.gevCDF ξ).measure =
    ((↑r + 1) ^ ξ * Real.Gamma (1 - ξ) - 1) / (ξ * (↑r + 1))
scope_note: Standard law, xi < 1, xi != 0. The case xi = 0 is the separate entry gumbel-pwm.

name: Probability-weighted moments of the Gumbel law
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.integral_mul_gevFun_pow_gevCDF_zero (r : ℕ) :
  ∫ (x : ℝ), x * ExtremeValueTheory.gevFun 0 x ^ r ∂(ExtremeValueTheory.gevCDF 0).measure =
    (Real.eulerMascheroniConstant + Real.log (↑r + 1)) / (↑r + 1)
scope_note: Standard law.

name: The return level is the (1-1/m) quantile of H_xi
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.gevFun_returnLevel (ξ : ℝ) {m : ℝ} (hm : 1 < m) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.gevFun ξ (ExtremeValueTheory.returnLevel ξ m) = 1 - 1 / m
scope_note: Standard law, m > 1. Inference for return levels is in the likelihood area.

name: Weak convergence on R through Mathlib's cdf
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.tendsto_probabilityMeasure_iff_forall_continuousAt_tendsto_cdf
  {μs : ℕ → MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure ℝ} {μ : MeasureTheory.ProbabilityMeasure ℝ} :
  Filter.Tendsto μs Filter.atTop (nhds μ) ↔
    ∀ (x : ℝ),
      ContinuousAt (↑(ProbabilityTheory.cdf ↑μ)) x →
        Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(ProbabilityTheory.cdf ↑(μs n)) x) Filter.atTop
          (nhds (↑(ProbabilityTheory.cdf ↑μ) x))
scope_note: The converse direction is proved in this library (Mathlib has no such statement at this version), so it is not a wrapper. Sequences only.

name: X has law F.measure iff F is its c.d.f.
scope_note: Restates Mathlib's correspondence between a law on R and its c.d.f. for the library's CumulativeDistributionFunction; no mathematics of its own.

name: The law of the c.d.f. of a probability measure is that measure
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.measure_ofMeasure (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ)
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] : (CumulativeDistributionFunction.ofMeasure μ).measure = μ
scope_note: One-line restatement of Mathlib's ProbabilityTheory.measure_cdf for the library's CumulativeDistributionFunction.

name: Poisson limit of the k-th largest order statistic
scope_note: orderStat x j is the (j+1)-th largest, so the indices are shifted by one against the books.

name: Limit law of the normalized k-th largest order statistic
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.tendsto_measureReal_affine_orderStat_le.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
  (hX : ∀ (i : ℕ), Measurable (X i)) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X P)
  {F G : CumulativeDistributionFunction}
  (hF : ∀ (i : ℕ) (x : ℝ), P.real {ω | X i ω ≤ x} = ↑F.toStieltjesFunction x)
  {As : ℕ → AffineIncrEquiv} {x : ℝ} (hGx : ↑G.toStieltjesFunction x ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1)
  (h :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑(As n • F).toStieltjesFunction x ^ n) Filter.atTop
      (nhds (↑G.toStieltjesFunction x)))
  (j : ℕ) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun n => P.real {ω | (As n) (ExtremeValueTheory.orderStat (fun i => X (↑i) ω) j) ≤ x})
    Filter.atTop
    (nhds
      (↑G.toStieltjesFunction x *
        ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (j + 1), (-Real.log (↑G.toStieltjesFunction x)) ^ m / ↑m.factorial))
scope_note: Only at points x with H(x) in (0,1): the boundary of the support is excluded by hypothesis, whereas the book states the limit for every x.

name: Joint limit law of the two largest order statistics
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.tendsto_measureReal_orderStat_zero_le_and_orderStat_one_le.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1}
  [MeasurableSpace Ω] {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P]
  {X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (hX : ∀ (i : ℕ), Measurable (X i)) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X P)
  {F : ℝ → ℝ} (hF : ∀ (i : ℕ) (x : ℝ), P.real {ω | X i ω ≤ x} = F x) {u v : ℕ → ℝ}
  (hvu : ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, v n ≤ u n) {τ₁ τ₂ : ℝ}
  (hu : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑n * (1 - F (u n))) Filter.atTop (nhds τ₁))
  (hv : Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ↑n * (1 - F (v n))) Filter.atTop (nhds τ₂)) :
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun n =>
      P.real
        {ω |
          ExtremeValueTheory.orderStat (fun i => X (↑i) ω) 0 ≤ u n ∧
            ExtremeValueTheory.orderStat (fun i => X (↑i) ω) 1 ≤ v n})
    Filter.atTop (nhds (Real.exp (-τ₂) * (1 + τ₂ - τ₁)))
scope_note: Two levels only. The cited theorem gives the joint law of any number of upper order statistics.

name: Rényi: P(record at k) = 1/k
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.measureReal_isRecord.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
  (hX : ∀ (i : ℕ), Measurable (X i)) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X P)
  (hident : ∀ (i : ℕ), MeasureTheory.Measure.map (X i) P = MeasureTheory.Measure.map (X 0) P)
  (hcont : ∀ (x : ℝ), P {ω | X 0 ω = x} = 0) (k : ℕ) :
  P.real {ω | ExtremeValueTheory.IsRecord (fun i => X i ω) k} = 1 / (↑k + 1)
scope_note: Continuity of F is stated as no atoms. Indices start at 0, so the probability at index k is 1/(k+1).

name: Weak law of large numbers for the number of records
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.tendstoInMeasure_recordCount_div_log.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ}
  (hX : ∀ (i : ℕ), Measurable (X i)) (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X P)
  (hident : ∀ (i : ℕ), MeasureTheory.Measure.map (X i) P = MeasureTheory.Measure.map (X 0) P)
  (hcont : ∀ (x : ℝ), P {ω | X 0 ω = x} = 0) :
  MeasureTheory.TendstoInMeasure P
    (fun n ω => ↑(ExtremeValueTheory.recordCount (fun i => X i ω) n) / Real.log ↑n) Filter.atTop
    fun x => 1
scope_note: Convergence in probability only; the strong law and the CLT for N_n are not stated.
